main.content: ==English== ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|apparaunt}}, {{m|enm|aparaunt}}, from {{der|en|fro|aparent}}, {{m|fro|aparant}}, in turn from {{der|en|la|appārēns|appārēns, appārentis}}, present participle of {{m|la|appāreō}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/əˈpæɹənt/|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/əˈpæɹənt/|a=GA,nMmmm}} * {{IPA|en|/əˈpɛɹənt/|a=GA,Mmmm}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-apparent.ogg|a=US,Mmmm}} * {{IPA|en|/əˈpaɾənt/|a=Scotland,Wales}} ===Adjective=== {{en-adj}} # Capable of being [[seen]], or easily seen; open to [[view]]; visible to the eye; within [[sight]] or view. #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=IV|text=[…] Hesperus, that led / The starry host, rode brightest, till the moon, / Rising in clouded majesty, at length / '''Apparent''' queen unveiled her peerless light, / And o’er the dark her silver mantle threw.|year=1873}} #: {{ux|en|Her disappointment was '''apparent''' to everyone.}} #: {{ux|en|The '''apparent''' cause of the fire was faulty wiring.}} #: {{co|en|make '''apparent'''}} #: {{co|en|become '''apparent'''}} #: {{co|en|for no '''apparent''' reason}} # Clear or [[manifest]] to the understanding; plain; [[evident]]; [[obvious]]; known; palpable; indubitable. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King John|IV|2|text=Salisbury: It is '''apparent''' foul-play; and ’tis shame / That greatness should so grossly offer it: / So thrive it in your game! and so, farewell.}} #* {{RQ:Stoker Dracula|20|text=When I came to Renfield's room I found him lying on the floor on his left side in a glittering pool of blood. When I went to move him, it became at once '''apparent''' that he had received some terrible injuries.}} # {{senseid|en|nonreal}} Appearing to the eye or mind (distinguished from, but not necessarily opposed to, true or real); seeming. #* '''1785,''' {{w|Thomas Reid}}, ''Essays on the Intellectual Powers of Man'', Essay II (“Of the Powers we have by means of our External Senses”), Chapter XIX (“Of Matter and of Space”), #*: What {{w|George Berkeley}} calls visible magnitude was by astronomers called '''apparent''' magnitude. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1848|author=[[w:Thomas Babington Macaulay, 1st Baron Macaulay|Thomas Babington Macaulay]]|title=w:The History of England from the Accession of James the Second |passage=To live on terms of civility, and even of '''apparent''' friendship.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1911|author=w:Encyclopædia Britannica|title=[[s:1911 Encyclopædia Britannica/Aberration|Aberration]] |passage=This '''apparent''' motion is due to the finite velocity of light, and the progressive motion of the observer with the earth, as it performs its yearly course about the sun.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847 |title=Boundary problems|url=http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21582498-america-has-changed-way-it-measures-gdp-boundary-problems |passage=Economics is a messy discipline: too fluid to be a science, too rigorous to be an art. Perhaps it is fitting that economists’ most-used metric, gross domestic product (GDP), is a tangle too. GDP measures the total value of output in an economic territory. Its '''apparent''' simplicity explains why it is scrutinised down to tenths of a percentage point every month.}} ====Usage notes==== * The word {{m|en||apparent}} has two common uses that are almost in opposition. One means roughly “clear; clearly true”, and serves to make a statement ''more'' decisive: *: ''It was '''apparent''' that no one knew the answer.'' (=No one knew the answer, and it showed.) * The other is roughly “seeming; to all appearances”, and serves to make a statement ''less'' decisive: *: ''The '''apparent''' source of the hubbub was a stray kitten.'' (=There was a stray kitten, and it seemed to be the source of the hubbub.) * These uses can be consistently distinguished: it has the "clear" sense when used as a predicate, and the "seemingly" sense when used attributively, as above. * The same ambivalence occurs with the derived adverb {{m|en|apparently}}, which usually means “seemingly” but can also mean “clearly”, especially when it is modified by another adverb, such as {{m|en|quite}}. ====Synonyms==== * {{sense|easy to see}} {{l|en|visible}}, {{l|en|conspicuous}}, {{l|en|distinct}}, {{l|en|plain}}, {{l|en|obvious}}, {{l|en|clear}}, {{l|en|eyely}} * {{sense|easy to understand}} {{l|en|distinct}}, {{l|en|plain}}, {{l|en|obvious}}, {{l|en|clear}}, {{l|en|certain}}, {{l|en|evident}}, {{l|en|manifest}}, {{l|en|indubitable}}, {{l|en|notorious}}, {{l|en|transparent}}, {{l|en|prima facie}} * {{sense|seeming to be the case}} {{l|en|illusory}}, {{l|en|superficial}} ====Antonyms==== * {{antsense|within
